text.p: The mark showed no sign of leaving its established trading ranges, taking little notice of another bout of EMU-related comments, traders said.

The Swedish crown was active though, reconquering some of the ground lost amid concern about Sweden's expansionary budget. A Swedish finance ministry spokesman said growth could be better than forecast in the budget on Tuesday because of an expected improvement in the country's export performance.
"The focus is back on Sweden's fiscal policy, and they seem to be going in the opposite direction than the rest of Europe, fiscally speaking," said David Coleman at CIBC Wood Gundy.
Sweden's spring budget announcement forecast a balanced budget for 1998 and not a surplus as previously forecast.

The lira and the peseta were unfazed by a report in Italian financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore, which cited sources in Bonn saying a deal was taking shape between France and Germany to keep Spain and Italy out of the first wave of EMU.

Senior Italian, French and German officials denied the report, with Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi saying there were no such "secret deals" and a French Finance Ministry official saying such a deal was "completely absurd". German Finance Minister Theo Waigel also said there were no such plans.

Waigel said Germany still had a chance to meet the three percent EMU budget deficit target, and dismissed speculation about relaxed budget deficit-to-GDP criteria. He said "3.0 is 3.0", in reference to the budget requirement.
"I think the market wants to see some numbers coming in first to judge whether the EMU qualification interpretation will be loose or not," Bank America chief European economist Jeremy Hawkins said.
The Bundesbank said in its monthly report it saw no indication investors were pulling out of mark investments in response to EMU uncertainty.--London forex desk +44 171 542 7791
